notes: The day was spent recovering the studio's production build and stabilizing its dependencies after an update had broken both the build and the studio's appearance. To keep the studio usable during the investigation, the live site was first pointed back to the last working deployment so editors could keep working without errors. The local build failures were then traced through two separate causes — missing project configuration during the build, and a media plugin that could no longer load a required library — while the changed studio look was tracked down to a dependency update that had pulled in the latest content editor instead of the intended older version that matches production. The fix restored the dependency lock file to the last known working state, kept the compatible older media plugin, and reinstalled only the newly required packages, after clearing the package cache to get past a disk-space error. A clean build with no remaining warnings or errors confirmed the studio was fully recovered.

notes:
1. Investigated a report that ChatGPT could not read the full content of a case study page — confirmed the live page was serving only the navigation, footer, and page title to AI crawlers, leaving the actual story invisible to them.
  2. Traced the root cause: the older case study layout waited for a browser-side data lookup (used only to build the previous and next story links) before showing anything, so the version of the page sent to crawlers had an empty body.
  3. Fixed the issue by preparing the case study content and the previous/next story links ahead of time when the page is built, so the complete story is now included in the page exactly as served.
  4. Removed the unnecessary data request that previously ran in every visitor's browser just to build two navigation links, which also lightens the page for regular visitors.
  5. Verified the fix locally: the readable text on the page grew from roughly 600 characters to over 5,600, with all key story details present without needing JavaScript — this fix covers every case study using the older layout, not just the reported one.
  6. Confirmed the change introduced no new code-quality errors by comparing automated checks before and after the change.
  7. Audited the rest of the site for the same problem and found the blog, resources, knowledge base, and case studies listing pages, plus author pages, build their lists in the visitor's browser — leaving them nearly empty for crawlers that don't run JavaScript.
  8. Confirmed individual blog posts, knowledge base articles, and newer-style case studies were unaffected — they already serve their full content.
  9. Confirmed the site's AI-companion pages and AI-readable site guide already make the case studies listing readable to AI tools, matching a separate validation of that page.
  10. Deployed the fix and validated it on both the local and live pages, including before-and-after ChatGPT sessions shared as proof that the page is now fully readable.
